stories.headline: Stray Ukrainian drones collapse Latvia's coalition: Siliņa resigns, Kulbergs nominated to form government
stories.summary: A series of Ukrainian drones that crossed into Latvian airspace on May 7 and struck an oil storage facility in Rēzekne triggered a political chain reaction: PM Siliņa fired Defence Minister Sprūds on May 10, the Progressives withdrew coalition support on May 13, Siliņa resigned on May 14, and President Rinkēvičs conducted two rounds of consultations before nominating opposition United List lawmaker Andris Kulbergs to form a new government on May 16. NATO fighters tracked but did not intercept a second drone; Russia promoted a 'Zelensky curse' narrative; Agriculture Minister Krauze was also briefly suspended after a KNAB search on the morning of the resignation. New Unity has stated its 'red lines' for coalition talks, the Progressives are prepared to sit in opposition until October elections, and a political analyst has questioned whether Kulbergs can assemble a viable majority.

stories.headline: KNAB searches agriculture minister Krauze in forestry sector corruption case on morning of PM's resignation
stories.summary: On the morning of May 14 — the same morning PM Siliņa announced her resignation — KNAB investigators acting on prosecutors' orders searched Agriculture Minister Armands Krauze (Union of Greens and Farmers) and detained him briefly as part of the so-called 'timber industry' (kokrūpnieku) criminal case. Krauze was released the same day; Siliņa had suspended him from office before her resignation. The Progressives said they intend to ensure the corruption case stays on the political agenda regardless of which coalition forms next.

stories.headline: Bank of Latvia issues Latvia's first dual MiCA and PSD2 licences to crypto exchange Paybis
stories.summary: Latvia's central bank (Latvijas Banka) issued two licences to SIA Paybis Europe on May 12: a MiCA crypto-asset service provider licence and a PSD2 payment institution licence, making Paybis the first firm in Latvia to hold both simultaneously. The licences allow Paybis to offer crypto services across all 27 EU member states and the EEA. Paybis CEO cited Latvia's regulatory framework as a deliberate choice.
